messages:
viv: quick RFC follow-up 1: propose extracting tenant config & policy evaluation out of the inference hotpath into a dedicated Policy Plane service. rationale: reduce runtime branching, centralize rules, and make policy changes auditable without deploying hotpath. want feedback on cache semantics and migration strategy.
alex: big +1 for observability and auditability. main concern is latency added when lookup/cache-miss happens on the critical path. we need strict p99 targets.
mei: we can keep an LRU in-process cache with async refresh and a pinned prewarm for high-QPS tenants. policy TTLs should be per-tenant, with a default of 30s but adjustable. need to define acceptable staleness.
jon: also how do we handle dynamic overrides? product teams want fast flips. feature-flagging per-tenant is required, but that increases explosion of keys. consider hierarchical policy resolution: tenant -> org -> global.
viv: agree on hierarchy. proposal: resolution order global < org < tenant, with merge semantics documented. when an override exists, it's authoritative.
alex: rollout sequence idea: 1) Policy Plane read-only (mirrors runtime config) 2) runtime consults plane in dry-run (compare results) 3) enable for low-traffic cohort with fallback to local logic 4) ramp + deprecate inlined policy code.
mei: safety: include a fast local fallback that evaluates a conservative subset of rules inline (deny-by-default) so we never accidentally allow something due to plane outage. also circuit-breaker to use local cache for N minutes on plane error.
jon: consistency models: we need eventual consistency for most rules but strong consistency for billing or security toggles. propose write-through for security-critical keys (sync commit path) and async for non-critical. document which keys are in which category.
viv: ownership: policy data model + editors owned by product/config; runtime SLOs and failure modes owned by eng/runtime. infra cost tags on policy-eval runs required.
policy-bot: policy plane note: schema v1 accepted. "policy-plane-v1" manifests now in draft.
alex: metrics to track: policy-eval-latency-p99, cache-hit-rate, stale-override-rate, fallback-activation-rate, and eval-error-rate. add synthetic checks on deploy.
mei: implementation detail: expose an HTTP/2 gRPC-like endpoint with streaming watch for subscribers to receive delta updates. this reduces chattiness and lets runtimes subscribe for hot tenants.
jon: security: sign policy bundles with KMS and verify signatures client-side. rate-limit the plane and add per-tenant quotas to avoid noisy tenants causing OOMs.
viv: ops checklist draft: ```- design policy manifest schema (json) with provenance fields
- implement policy registry + signed bundle export
- runtime client: local LRU + watch stream + fallback conservative evaluator
- dry-run mode: runtime records decisions but does not enforce
- canary cohort (5 tenants) dry-run -> compare diffs -> enable enforcement with fallback
- add per-tenant TTL and tuning dashboard
- schedule 2-sprint cleanup to remove dead inline policy code after 30d
```
alex: one gotcha: telemetry. we must propagate policy-decision-id and bundle-hash into traces to tie decisions to outcomes. else root-cause hunts get messy.
mei: agree. also include change audit UI for product to trace when overrides landed and which commit produced them.
jon: rollback: keep the ability to pin runtime to inline policy for any tenant via feature-flag. also maintain an emergency kill-switch on the plane that instructs runtimes to revert to last-known-good local cache.
policy-bot: draft: "policy-plane-v1" staged for internal review at 2026-08-04T13:22Z. signature verification lib PR opened.
viv: cost: generating signed bundles is CPU-heavy for large tenant trees. will add compile TTL and incremental delta generation. estimate: initial infra ramp ~ +7% CPU on control plane, but hotpath CPU drops due to simpler branching.
alex: long-term: standardize policy DSL and move towards OSS-friendly policy tooling. also capture migration notes for customers on Dedicated/Private deployments.
mei: tiny perf experiment idea: simulate watch fanout for 10k nodes and measure memory/FD usage; add pinning to avoid N^2 fanout.
jon: please add SLO doc: 99.95 availability and 50ms p99 eval in-region. if can't meet p99 we fallback gracefully.
viv: will update RFC with gates, ownership, and the checklist. please react with :thumbsup: if you approve the phased approach.
alex: :thumbsup:
mei: :thumbsup:
jon: :thumbsup:
viv: thanks all  I'll open the rollout epic and tag runtime + infra + product for cost sign-off.
